page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 server family. It is equipped with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The system features 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The Intel Xeon processor's support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions contributes to strong results in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory performance is also strong for large block read and write operations, though single-core performance and small-block cached memory bandwidth remain in the average tier.

This server configuration is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and software compilation, as evidenced by strong Passmark database and Clang compilation benchmarks. It also performs well in static web serving and prompt processing for smaller language models. However, it exhibits weak performance in text generation for large 70B parameter models due to the lack of GPU acceleration. The inclusion of substantial local storage and high memory capacity makes it a cost-effective option for resource-dense, non-GPU general-purpose enterprise applications.

Operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, this server includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth for large blocks, and strong database operations. It excels in multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, and static web serving. However, single-core performance is average, and the lack of a GPU results in weak text generation speeds for large language models. This instance is best suited for enterprise databases, multi-threaded applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring high local storage capacity.
